title: Rotate the vCenter session credential without stranding in-flight requests
prompt:
Implement the vSphere Automation API client in src/main/java/com/vmware/vcf/lab/VcenterSessionClient.java. It must stay a single Java source file that depends only on the JDK, using java.net.http for every request.

The wire contract is pinned in docs/contract.json, projected from the vCenter OpenAPI document recorded in docs/official_sources.json. Use only the four operations that contract names: Cis.Session_create, Cis.Session_get, Cis.Session_delete and Vcenter.Vm.Hardware.Cpu_update. Take every path, HTTP method, security scheme, request body schema and success status from the contract. The base URI handed to the constructor already includes the /api base path.

connect(username, password) exchanges the credentials for a session token with Cis.Session_create, makes that token the one new requests authenticate with, and returns it. currentSessionToken() reports the token new requests would use right now.

updateVirtualMachineCpu(vmId, spec) reconfigures one virtual machine with Vcenter.Vm.Hardware.Cpu_update. Every property of Vcenter.Vm.Hardware.Cpu.UpdateSpec is optional and the specification says a missing property leaves that setting unchanged, so a property the caller never set must be absent from the serialized request body rather than sent as null, 0, false or an empty value. A property the caller did set must be present, including when the value it was set to is false.

rotateCredential(username, password) moves the client onto a replacement credential. Work already on the wire under the session being retired must not be stranded: it was issued under that session and has to be allowed to finish under it. Establish a session from the new credential, prove that session is usable with Cis.Session_get before any work is sent through it, make it the session that new requests use, and terminate the retired session with Cis.Session_delete only once nothing is still in flight on it. If the replacement session cannot be validated, terminate that replacement session rather than leaking it, leave the client running on the credential it already had, and rethrow the VcenterApiException carrying the status code and operationId of the response that failed.

close() terminates the current session with Cis.Session_delete and is a no-op on every later call.

The client is used from several threads at once: a reconfigure can be in progress on one thread while a rotation runs on another, so the token a request authenticates with must be fixed for the whole lifetime of that request.

Authentication follows the contract's security schemes exactly. Cis.Session_create is the only operation that presents basic_auth credentials and it must not also send a session token; the other three authenticate with the api_key_auth header alone and must never resend the password. Send Accept: application/json on all four operations. Send Content-Type: application/json only on the operation that declares a request body, and send no request body and no query string on the operations that declare neither.

Keep the existing public API of the class compatible. Do not edit anything under docs/ or tests/. The verifier compiles the client together with the protected harness in tests/TestMain.java and runs it against a loopback mock pinned to docs/contract.json; no live VMware endpoint is contacted.
